```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yamaguchi_2024_cefiderocol"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yamaguchi_2024_cefiderocol"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/prp2.70001> (open access; PMC11343721)

Yamaguchi 2024 is a stochastic simulation and estimation (SSE) study that asks
how many neonates and infants a pediatric cefiderocol trial needs to estimate
the pediatric PK parameters with acceptable precision. The "true" model that
generates every simulated dataset is the pediatric cefiderocol PK model of
Katsube 2019 (IDWeek abstract), printed in full as Equations 1-4 and the
"True Value" column of Table 4. That model is what is packaged here: a
two-compartment model whose CL, V1, Q and V2 scale with body weight using
the beta-lactam class exponents of Shimamura 2007 (0.578 for clearances, 0.677
for volumes), with the Rhodin 2009 glomerular-filtration maturation function of
postmenstrual age on CL.

# Population

No pediatric subject was observed in the source. Each simulated design
contained virtual neonates, infants, toddlers, children and adolescents
(Groups 1-10 of Table 1; Groups A-J of Table 2), 1:1 female:male, with
gestational age (GA) and postnatal age (PNA) uniform within each group and
body weight generated from age by published weight-for-age relationships, plus
the observed plasma concentrations of 516 adults (healthy subjects and
patients) from five cefiderocol clinical studies as Group 11. Dosing was a
single 3-h infusion adjusted by PNA, GA and body weight (Table S1). The model
itself is the pediatric projection of the adult cefiderocol popPK, so it is a
prediction model for children rather than a fit to pediatric data.

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yamaguchi_2024_cefiderocol"))$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` | log(0.508) L/h at 1 kg | Equation 1; Table 4 'True Value' |
| `lvc` | log(0.460) L at 1 kg | Equation 2; Table 4 |
| `lq` | log(0.495) L/h at 1 kg | Equation 3; Table 4 |
| `lvp` | log(0.318) L at 1 kg | Equation 4; Table 4 |
| `e_wt_cl_q` | 0.578 (fixed) | Equations 1 and 3; Table 4 'Power on CL and Q'; from Shimamura 2007 (ref 21) |
| `e_wt_vc_vp` | 0.677 (fixed) | Equations 2 and 4; Table 4 'Power on V1 and V2'; from Shimamura 2007 |
| `tmat50` | 47.7 weeks (fixed) | Methods 'Pharmacokinetic model'; Table 4 'TM50'; from Rhodin 2009 (refs 22-23) |
| `hill_mat` | 3.4 (fixed) | Methods 'Pharmacokinetic model'; Table 4 'HILL' |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc`, `etalvp` | 0.040 each | Methods (log-normal, 20% CV); Table 4 'BSV_CL', 'BSV_V1', 'BSV_V2' |
| `propSd` | 0.20 | Table 4 'RUVprop' = 0.040, read as a variance |
| CL = 0.508 x BW^0.578 x PMA^HILL / (PMA^HILL + TM50^HILL) | n/a | Equation 1 |
| V1 = 0.460 x BW^0.677; Q = 0.495 x BW^0.578; V2 = 0.318 x BW^0.677 | n/a | Equations 2-4 |
| Two-compartment disposition, IV infusion into central | n/a | Methods 'Pharmacokinetic model' and 'Simulation' |

# Virtual cohort

The cohort reproduces Design #1 (Table 1, Groups 1-10), the design shown in
Supplementary Figure S1, at 30 subjects per neonate/infant group and 50 per
older group instead of the paper's 3 and 6 per group (times 300 datasets).

Body weight is generated from postmenstrual age. Up to 40 weeks the median is
an intrauterine birth-weight curve; after term it is a sex-averaged
weight-for-age median indexed by age since 40 weeks. Individual weights are
log-normal around the median with a 12% CV. See "Assumptions and deviations"
for why this differs from the paper's weight model.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20241101)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241101)

# Sex-averaged median body weight (kg) by postmenstrual age (weeks).
# PMA <= 40: intrauterine growth; PMA > 40: weight-for-age at
# (PMA - 40) weeks of corrected age.
wt_ref <- tibble::tribble(
  ~pma_wk, ~wt_kg,
  24, 0.65, 26, 0.90, 28, 1.15, 30, 1.45, 32, 1.80, 34, 2.25,
  36, 2.75, 38, 3.15, 40, 3.50,
  40 + 4.35, 4.35, 40 + 8.7, 5.35, 40 + 13.0, 6.10, 40 + 26.1, 7.60,
  40 + 39.1, 8.55, 40 + 52.2, 9.25, 40 + 78.3, 10.6, 40 + 104.4, 11.85,
  40 + 156.5, 14.1, 40 + 208.7, 16.2, 40 + 260.9, 18.2, 40 + 313.1, 20.3,
  40 + 417.4, 25.5, 40 + 521.8, 32.0, 40 + 626.2, 40.5, 40 + 730.5, 50.0,
  40 + 834.9, 57.0, 40 + 939.2, 62.0
)
median_wt <- function(pma_wk) {
  exp(approx(wt_ref$pma_wk, log(wt_ref$wt_kg), xout = pma_wk, rule = 2)$y)
}

# Design #1 age groups (Table 1). PNA in days; GA in weeks.
groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~ga_lo, ~ga_hi, ~pna_lo, ~pna_hi, ~n,
  1, 26, 32, 0, 14, 30,
  2, 26, 32, 14, 28, 30,
  3, 32, 37, 0, 14, 30,
  4, 32, 37, 14, 28, 30,
  5, 37, 40, 0, 28, 30,
  6, 26, 44, 28, 91.3, 30,
  7, 40, 40, 91.3, 730.5, 50,
  8, 40, 40, 730.5, 2191.5, 50,
  9, 40, 40, 2191.5, 4383, 50,
  10, 40, 40, 4383, 6574.5, 50
)

subj <- groups |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::reframe(
    group = group,
    GA = runif(n, ga_lo, ga_hi),
    PNA_d = runif(n, pna_lo, pna_hi)
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    PAGE = GA + PNA_d / 7,
    WT = median_wt(PAGE) * exp(rnorm(dplyr::n(), 0, sqrt(log(1 + 0.12^2)))),
    panel = ifelse(group <= 6, "PNA < 3 months", "PNA 3 months to < 18 years"),
    # Table S1 dosing, 3-h infusion
    dose_mg = dplyr::case_when(
      PNA_d < 61 & GA < 32 ~ 30 * WT,
      PNA_d < 61 ~ 40 * WT,
      PNA_d < 91.3 & GA < 32 ~ 40 * WT,
      PNA_d < 91.3 ~ 60 * WT,
      WT < 34 ~ 60 * WT,
      TRUE ~ 2000
    )
  )

subj |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    `PMA (weeks)` = sprintf("%.1f-%.1f", min(PAGE), max(PAGE)),
    `Median WT (kg)` = round(median(WT), 2),
    `Median dose (mg)` = round(median(dose_mg))
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Virtual Design #1 cohort.")
```

```{r events}
# Sampling: 3, 5, 8 h for Groups 1-8; 1, 3, 3.5, 5, 8 h for Groups 9-10
# (Table 1 note). A rich grid is added for NCA.
sparse_times <- function(group) if (group >= 9) c(1, 3, 3.5, 5, 8) else c(3, 5, 8)
rich_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 3, by = 0.25), seq(3.5, 12, by = 0.5), seq(13, 48, by = 1))))

make_events <- function(s, obs_fun) {
  dose_rows <- s |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      id, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose_mg, rate = dose_mg / 3,
      cmt = "central", WT, PAGE, group, panel
    )
  obs_rows <- s |>
    dplyr::rowwise() |>
    dplyr::reframe(
      id = id, time = obs_fun(group), evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0,
      cmt = "central", WT = WT, PAGE = PAGE, group = group, panel = panel
    )
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    as.data.frame()
}

ev_sparse <- make_events(subj, sparse_times)
ev_rich <- make_events(subj, function(g) rich_times)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_sparse[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Yamaguchi_2024_cefiderocol")
sim_sparse <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_sparse, keep = c("group", "panel")) |>
  as.data.frame()
sim_rich <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod |> rxode2::zeroRe("sigma"),
  events = ev_rich, keep = c("group", "panel")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Replicate Supplementary Figure S1

Supplementary Figure S1 shows box plots of the simulated concentrations at each
sampling time for Design #1, split at PNA 3 months. Times 1 and 3.5 h are
sampled only in Groups 9 and 10. The simulated observations below include the
proportional residual error (`sim` column).

```{r figure-s1, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
# The sparse solve has no time-zero observation, so every row is a sample.
fig_s1 <- sim_sparse |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    panel = factor(panel, levels = c("PNA < 3 months", "PNA 3 months to < 18 years")),
    time_f = factor(time, levels = c(1, 3, 3.5, 5, 8))
  )

ggplot(fig_s1, aes(time_f, sim)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after the start of infusion (h)",
    y = "Plasma cefiderocol (ug/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Supplementary Figure S1 of Yamaguchi 2024 (Design #1)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The medians are compared below with the medians read off Supplementary
Figure S1 by the maintainers (box centre lines; reading precision about
2 ug/mL).

```{r figure-s1-compare}
published_s1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~panel, ~time, ~median_pub,
  "PNA < 3 months", 3, 132,
  "PNA < 3 months", 5, 83,
  "PNA < 3 months", 8, 51,
  "PNA 3 months to < 18 years", 1, 61,
  "PNA 3 months to < 18 years", 3, 97,
  "PNA 3 months to < 18 years", 3.5, 71,
  "PNA 3 months to < 18 years", 5, 33,
  "PNA 3 months to < 18 years", 8, 11
)

s1_cmp <- fig_s1 |>
  dplyr::group_by(panel = as.character(panel), time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_sim = median(sim), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(published_s1, by = c("panel", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (median_sim / median_pub - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(s1_cmp) == nrow(published_s1))

s1_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(median_sim = round(median_sim, 1), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Panel" = panel, "Time (h)" = time,
    "Simulated median (ug/mL)" = median_sim,
    "Figure S1 median (ug/mL)" = median_pub,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median concentrations: simulation vs Supplementary Figure S1.")
```

The 3 months to < 18 years panel is reproduced to within about 10% at all
five sampling times. The < 3 months panel is not: the simulated medians are
about 60% lower than Figure S1 at 3, 5 and 8 h alike. That panel cannot be
produced by Equations 1-4 with the Table S1 doses. Its 3-h median of
132 ug/mL is well above dose / (V1 + V2), the concentration the dose would
give with no elimination at all, for the typical subject of every neonatal and
infant group (see the table below). A uniform factor of about 2.6 at every
time point would also mean a neonatal AUC about 2.6 times that of older
children, which contradicts the paper's statement that the Table S1 doses give
comparable drug exposure. The packaged model reproduces that statement (next
section). The neonatal panel is therefore listed as a known deviation and is
excluded from the gate below; it is shown in the table above so the
disagreement stays visible.

```{r figure-s1-ceiling}
ceiling_tab <- sim_rich |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, group, vc, vp) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    ev_rich |> dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |> dplyr::select(id, amt),
    by = "id"
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ceiling = round(median(amt / (vc + vp)), 1), .groups = "drop")
ceiling_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Group" = group, "Median dose / (V1 + V2) (ug/mL)" = ceiling) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "No-elimination concentration ceiling by Design #1 group.")
stopifnot(all(ceiling_tab$ceiling[ceiling_tab$group <= 6] < 132))
```

```{r figure-s1-gate}
# Gate on the reproduced panel only. Centre and robust envelope over its
# five time points: a mis-transcribed coefficient, exponent or dose moves
# every median by tens of percent; the remaining spread comes from the
# weight-for-age curve, the cohort draw and the reading of the figure
# (about 2 ug/mL, i.e. up to ~20% at the 11 ug/mL 8-h median). Realised
# -5% to +4% (default threads) and -9% to +3% (2 threads, another seed).
older <- s1_cmp |> dplyr::filter(panel == "PNA 3 months to < 18 years")
stopifnot(
  nrow(older) == 5,
  abs(median(older$pct_diff)) < 10,
  quantile(abs(older$pct_diff), 0.9) < 20
)
```

# Maturation and size

Typical clearance across the age range, with the Rhodin 2009 maturation
fraction that multiplies it.

```{r maturation, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
th <- ui$theta
fmat_fun <- function(pma) pma^th[["hill_mat"]] / (pma^th[["hill_mat"]] + th[["tmat50"]]^th[["hill_mat"]])
# Deterministic checks of Equation 1 at fixed covariates.
stopifnot(
  abs(fmat_fun(47.7) - 0.5) < 1e-12,
  abs(exp(th[["lcl"]]) * 70^th[["e_wt_cl_q"]] * fmat_fun(40 + 52 * 30) - 5.92) < 0.01
)

typ <- tibble::tibble(PAGE = seq(26, 40 + 52 * 18, length.out = 400)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    WT = median_wt(PAGE),
    fmat = fmat_fun(PAGE),
    CL = exp(th[["lcl"]]) * WT^th[["e_wt_cl_q"]] * fmat
  )
ggplot(typ, aes(PAGE / 52.18, CL / WT)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Postmenstrual age (years, log scale)",
    y = "Typical CL per kg (L/h/kg)",
    caption = "Equation 1 of Yamaguchi 2024 with the vignette weight-for-age curve."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA on the rich-grid solve (between-subject variability, no residual error),
by age group. The paper reports no NCA, so the check is internal: the
per-subject AUC0-inf from PKNCA must equal dose / CL.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_rich |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, group)

sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, group) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, group, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, group, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | group + id)
dose_df <- ev_rich |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, rate, group) |>
  dplyr::mutate(duration = amt / rate)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | group + id, duration = "duration")

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)

nca_tab |>
  dplyr::select(group, cmax, tmax, aucinf.obs, half.life) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = group, "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-inf (ug*h/mL)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (h)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated single-dose NCA by Design #1 age group (medians).")
```

```{r pknca-gate}
auc_chk <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::select(id, auc = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    sim_rich |> dplyr::distinct(id, cl),
    by = "id"
  ) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dose_df |> dplyr::select(id, amt), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auc / (amt / cl) - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(auc_chk) == nrow(subj))
# Methods 'Simulation': the Table S1 doses 'would provide comparable drug
# exposure' across ages. Every group's median AUC0-inf must sit within 35% of
# the pooled median (realised -15% to +18% here; a 2.6-fold neonatal shift,
# as Figure S1's left panel would imply, fails it).
auc_grp <- nca_tab$aucinf.obs / median(auc_chk$auc)
stopifnot(length(auc_grp) == 10, all(abs(auc_grp - 1) < 0.35))
# Same drawn parameters on both sides: the difference is trapezoidal and
# extrapolation error only.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(auc_chk$pct_diff)) < 2,
  quantile(abs(auc_chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 4
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Weight-for-age.** The paper generated body weight from age with the
  relationships of Sumpter and Holford 2011 and Sy 2014, whose coefficients are
  not reproduced in the paper. The vignette uses approximate sex-averaged median
  weights (an intrauterine growth curve to 40 weeks PMA, then weight-for-age
  medians) with a 12% CV. This affects only the virtual cohort, not the model.
- **Cohort size.** Design #1 has 3 subjects per neonate/infant group and 6 per
  older group, repeated over 300 datasets. The vignette uses 30 and 50 per group
  in a single draw. Group 5 GA (37 to < 40 weeks) and the Group 6 PNA upper
  limit (91.3 days) were set so the PMA ranges match Table 1. GA was fixed at
  40 weeks for Groups 7-10 (Table 1).
- **Supplementary Figure S1, PNA < 3 months panel, not reproduced.** The
  simulated medians are about 60% below the figure at 3, 5 and 8 h, while the
  3 months to < 18 years panel agrees within about 10%. The figure's neonatal
  medians exceed the no-elimination ceiling dose / (V1 + V2) of the model as
  printed, and imply a neonatal exposure about 2.6 times that of older
  children, against the paper's statement that the Table S1 doses give
  comparable exposure (which the packaged model reproduces). Whatever produced
  the figure panel (a different dose, weight model or parameterisation for the
  youngest subjects) is not described in the paper; the model follows
  Equations 1-4 and Table 4 as printed. A uniform reading error is excluded:
  the figure's y-axis is linear with 50 ug/mL gridlines.
- **Residual error read as a variance.** Table 4 prints `RUVprop = 0.040` beside
  between-subject variances of 0.040 (20% CV), so it is read as sigma^2 = 0.04,
  a 20% proportional SD. That matches the adult cefiderocol model (20.5%,
  Kawaguchi 2021). Reading it as an SD of 0.04 would give a 4% residual error.
- **No variability on Q.** The paper puts between-subject variability on CL,
  V1 and V2 only.
- **What is fixed.** The allometric exponents (Shimamura 2007) and the
  maturation constants (Rhodin 2009) were taken from the literature and are
  wrapped in `fixed()`. The structural coefficients and the variance terms are
  the simulation model's own values and are left estimable, as they were in
  the paper's re-estimation step (Table 4).
- **Adult clearance.** Equation 1 gives a typical CL of 5.92 L/h for a 70-kg
  adult (maturation fraction about 1), higher than the 4.04 L/h of the adult
  model (Kawaguchi 2021) at its reference creatinine clearance of 83 mL/min.
  Under the adult model's creatinine-clearance exponent of 0.682, 5.92 L/h
  corresponds to a creatinine clearance of about 145 mL/min. The pediatric
  model has no renal-function covariate beyond maturation, so it describes
  children with age-appropriate renal function. Table S4 of the paper repeats
  the SSE with weight centred at 70 kg and adult values (CL 4.04, V1 7.78,
  Q 6.19, V2 5.77); that is a sensitivity analysis and is not packaged.
- **Piecewise allometry (Design #3).** The alternative model with separate
  pediatric exponents (0.75, 1) was used only to test whether a difference in
  allometric relationships could be detected, and is not packaged.
- No correction notice for this article was found in Europe PMC as of
  2026-10-30.
